definitions.explanation: A narrow street or alley behind or between buildings, often in older urban areas.

examples.japanese: {路地裏|ろじうら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: To go into a back alley.

examples.japanese: {路地裏|ろじうら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{居酒屋|いざかや}→居酒屋：09635_izakaya⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つけた→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧。
examples.english: I found a pub in a back alley.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{路地裏|ろじうら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{昔|むかし}ながら→昔ながら：26817_mukashinagara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: Old-fashioned shops line the back alleys of this town.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{路地|ろじ}→路地：06501_roji⟧ (alley) + ⟦{裏|うら}→裏：02178_ura⟧ (back, behind). Refers to narrow passages behind or between buildings in older urban areas.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Back alleys in Japanese cities often have a nostalgic atmosphere. Many hide small ⟦{居酒屋|いざかや}→居酒屋：09635_izakaya⟧ (pubs), ⟦{食堂|しょくどう}→食堂：01054_shokudou⟧ (eateries), and ⟦{個人|こじん}→個人：02758_kojin⟧⟦{商店|しょうてん}→商店：11841_shouten⟧ (family shops) that are hard to find from main streets. "Hidden gem" restaurants in {路地裏|ろじうら} are a popular topic in food media.
